sectionContext.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
sectionContext.claim: A case for rationality requires a demonstration even though a rational process can still lead to a false conclusion.
sectionContext.warrant: People, including audiences of a magician, can draw reasonable conclusions from the evidence available to them while being misled.
sectionContext.inference: Subjective reasonableness is not enough; justification needs an evidential demonstration tied to the claim.

sectionContext.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
sectionContext.claim: Faith used as a foundation cannot discriminate reliably among beliefs.
sectionContext.warrant: The same appeal can support incompatible denominations or morally abhorrent claims, whereas people with good reasons can present those reasons directly.
sectionContext.inference: A bare faith appeal is not a truth-tracking justification and should not inherit the rationality of evidence-based confidence.
